items.title: Beyond AlphaFold 3: a standardised benchmark of open-source co-folding models for antibody-antigen complexes, from docking accuracy to interaction specificity.
items.abstract: Co-folding models are increasingly used to predict antibody-antigen complexes for epitope mapping, candidate triage and structure-guided de novo design or engineering, yet the latest generation of these models has not been compared under standardized conditions. We benchmark AlphaFold 3, Protenix-v2, ESMFold2, ESMFold2-fast and OpenDDE on 200 test-set complexes (121 Fvs and 79 V H Hs) from SAbDab2-Bench, a newly curated dataset, and a reconstructed antibody-antigen subset of FoldBench, Ab-FoldBench. Using standardized inputs, sampling, and interface metrics that isolate the antibody-antigen interface, we compare docking accuracy, inference-time scaling, confidence-based candidate structure selection and sensitivity to interaction perturbations. OpenDDE achieved the highest median DockQ and docking pass rate, followed by Protenix-v2, although their difference was not statistically significant. Both models outperformed AlphaFold 3 on these measures, alongside offering fewer licensing restrictions on model and prediction use. We further find that model confidence was generally effective at identifying accurate predictions but showed model-dependent variations. To probe interaction specificity, which is essential for antibody design, we generated decoys through non-conservative interface mutations, and non-cognate antigen shuffling. Confidence decreased for both perturbations, but more consistently for non-cognate antigens than for interface mutations, with OpenDDE retaining comparatively high confidence for many decoys. items.title: Nab-paclitaxel fused with the de novo designed receptor binder exhibits enhanced tumor targeting and therapeutic efficacy.
items.abstract: Chemotherapy has been widely used in cancer treatment, but most of the chemotherapeutic drugs rely mainly on passive accumulation due to lack of target specificity, which may lead to systemic toxicity and limited clinical utility. Recent advances in artificial intelligence-based protein design provide new opportunities for developing precision therapeutics. Here we modify the albumin-bound paclitaxel (Nab-PTX), one of the most widely used drugs in chemotherapies, by applying the fusion proteins of albumin with the de novo designed protein binders targeting human EGFR or HER2. The resulting particles, EGFRmb-Nab-PTX and HER2mb-Nab-PTX, retain the similar physicochemical properties of Nab-PTX while acquiring the receptor-specific binding capacities. The in vitro assays show that both binder-modified Nab-PTX particles have increased uptake and inhibitory effects significantly in the cancer cell lines with high receptor expression levels. Furthermore, the data from a xenograft model, including tumor growth, excised tumor analysis, organ histology, and fluorescence imaging, show that the binder-modified Nab-PTX enhances tumor accumulation, improves tumor suppression, and may reduce off-target exposure compared with the conventional Nab-PTX, suggesting that they may have promising clinical potential in cancer treatment. Overall, this strategy provides an adaptable modular platform for generating albumin-based chemotherapeutic drugs with target specificities, which can be readily customized with diverse target binders to enable precise cancer therapies.

items.title: HEIWA: Hybrid Explicit-Implicit Water Attention Affects Force Field Accuracy in Structure-Based Protein Language Model ESM3.
items.abstract: Protein language models have achieved remarkable success in structure prediction and de novo design. However, their understanding of physical interactions remains limited. For structure-based models, we hypothesize that this limitation stems from the absence of explicit solvent modeling: water mediates hydrogen bonding, hydrophobic burial, and electrostatic interactions that govern protein thermodynamics and kinetics, yet current structure-based models treat proteins as if they exist in a vacuum. Using thermophilic protein classification as a proxy task for force-field awareness, per-residue logit mis-correlated with H-bonds as a destabilizing attribute and exhibits significant solvent-accessible surface area (SASA)-dependent error, despite high overall classification accuracy. These artifacts point to the water-protein interface as a source of systematic bias. To address this, we propose HEIWA (HybridExplicit-Implicit Water Attention), a novel attention module that injects solvent-mediated force-field information into static ESM3 residue embeddings via an all-query-to-all-key water-residue attention. Biophysics-guided model selection identifies configurations whose residue-level outputs are more consistent with the RMSF benchmark and selected biophysical attributes, while classification performance remains broadly comparable to the baseline. By forcing the model to predict the protein thermophilicity from the contributions of individual residues, HEIWA learns biophysical patterns that can be extended to SUPFAM absent from the training data set. items.title: Cooling fast and slow: Characterizing the effects of vitrification in cryo-EM and the subsequent recovery of equilibrium populations.
items.abstract: Single-particle cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM), a powerful class of techniques in structural biology with the potential to resolve molecular ensembles, requires that samples be vitrified to protect them from the high vacuum of the electron microscope. However, the effects of vitrification on biomolecular ensembles are unknown. To study them, we carried out extensive molecular dynamics simulations (over 50 ms) of the Trp-cage miniprotein at equilibrium and undergoing rapid cooling. We simulated seven cooling rates spanning three orders of magnitude, with the slowest coolings matching experimental rates. By inspecting molecular mobility and density-temperature trajectories for water with and without protein, we found that water vitrification is unaltered by the protein. To track protein conformation changes, and to relate them to kinetics, we made a Markov State Model (MSM) of Trp-cage from 5.4 ms of equilibrium sampling at 277 K. We observed that MSM states with a characteristic time longer than the duration of the nonequilibrium cooling tend to be more robust to artifacts induced by such cooling. Critically, although we observe that some states vanish in the equilibrium ensemble at 230 K, none do in our nonequilibrium cooled ensembles. To account for these perturbations, we developed a thermodynamic inference framework for recovering equilibrium populations from vitrified ensembles. These results indicate that cryo-EM has the capacity to be an accurate technique for the study of biomolecular ensembles.

items.title: QRxVision: Multimodal QR Encoding and Computer Vision for Domain-Specific Drug Discovery.
items.abstract: Computational approaches applied to the drug discovery pipeline are invaluable because of their overall speed or time to solution, sustainability, accessibility combined with ever improving accuracy. Furthermore, the high-throughput virtual screening supports practical sampling of the vast chemical space for target-relevant bioactive compounds that can be experimentally validated further downstream in the drug development process. The current paradigm being practiced in computer-aided drug screening strategies centers around structure-based and ligand-based approaches supported by a range of computational tools including de novo design, molecular dynamics-based approaches, and machine learning (ML). Overall, the latter approach has shown great promise generating models of high computational speed coupled with good accuracy. In this work, we developed QRxVision, a domain-specific multimodal ML model explicitly optimized for kinase target assignment using similarity-based profile matching and retrieval. QRxVision utilizes image vision from a pretrained VGG16 (Visual Geometry Group-16) model for deep spatial feature extraction and cosine similarity calculation. By encoding drug multimodality-associated parameters (MAP) into standardized QR code images, QRxVision can evaluate the similarity between test and reference compounds. Drug targets can then be assigned via transitive profile matching. items.title: Co-administration of the long-acting monoclonal antibody AZD7442 and bivalent Ancestral/BA.1 vaccination is well-tolerated in immunosuppressed patients highly vulnerable to infection with SARS-CoV-2 virus: the results of the multicentre, open-label, phase II randomised controlled, RAPID-PROTECTION trial
items.abstract: Abstract Immunocompromised individuals remain at risk of severe COVID-19. This multicentre, open-label, phase II randomised controlled trial evaluated the safety, pharmacokinetics and immunogenicity of co-administering the long-acting monoclonal antibody AZD7442 with a bivalent (Ancestral/BA.1) mRNA/LNP SARS-CoV-2 vaccine. A total of 139 immunocompromised adults received AZD7442 followed 28 days later by vaccination. AZD7442 was well tolerated, with no serious adverse events. Serum AZD7442 concentrations peaked at day 28 and remained detectable across disease cohorts at day 180. Anti-Spike antibody responses increased after AZD7442 and reached their highest levels after vaccination. Although binding antibodies against Omicron variants increased post-vaccination, neutralisation of Omicron remained limited after both AZD7442 and vaccination. Vaccination preferentially boosted antibodies targeting S2, the S1 N-terminal domain and receptor-binding domain epitopes not bound by AZD7442, and increased S2-specific memory B cells. Vaccine-induced T-cell responses were cross-reactive between ancestral and Omicron variants. Our findings support consideration of combined antibody and vaccine strategies in future therapeutic antibody development. The trial is registered with the International Standard Randomised Controlled Trial Number registry (ISRCTN53507177).

items.title: A Synthetic Benchmark for Topology-Aware Modeling of Multispecific Antibody Function.
items.abstract: Multispecific antibodies (msAbs) offer transformative therapeutic potential by engaging multiple epitopes simultaneously, yet their efficacy is an emergent property governed by complex molecular architectures. Rational design is often bottlenecked by the inability to predict how subtle changes in domain topology influence functional outcomes, a challenge exacerbated by the scarcity of comprehensive experimental data. Here, we introduce Synapse, a biologically inspired synthetic benchmark for topology-aware modeling of msAbs. First, we present a generative method that combines nonlinear per-domain sequence-to-score landscapes with connectivity-dependent synthetic readouts. Second, we propose a graph neural network architecture that explicitly encodes these topological constraints, distinguishing between format configurations that appear identical to the evaluated connectivity-agnostic multilayer perceptron. We demonstrate that this model learns topology-dependent structure-function relationships on synthetic landscapes and evaluate a transfer learning workflow as infrastructure for adaptation to biological datasets. We showcase our framework with a trispecific T cell engager-inspired synthetic topology-dependent optimization task and a constrained ranking of common light chain candidates against a composite objective. This work provides a controlled benchmarking environment for developing and evaluating topology-aware computational tools for msAb modeling. All experiments use synthetic data; no biological validation is performed.

items.title: Found: a protein that drives ageing without unleashing inflammation
Direct monitoring of breaching in deltaic submarine landslides
items.abstract: Submarine landslides threaten seabed infrastructure and trigger the transport of globally important amounts of sediment, carbon, and pollutants to deep-sea environments. However, fully submarine landslides have never been directly monitored in nature. Past hypotheses for their failure mechanism and dynamics therefore remain unvalidated for natural settings, including that prolonged upslope-migrating failures (breaching) occur in sandy seafloor environments. In this work, we present direct underwater monitoring of fully submarine landslides at Homathko Delta in western Canada that retrogress slowly upslope, indicating breaching-type failure. Their prolonged rather than instantaneous nature has important implications for the stress that seabed structures must be designed to withstand. Prolonged landslides also initiate sustained sediment flows (turbidity currents) that efficiently transport sediment, carbon, and pollutants further offshore.

items.title: Differentiation of stem-like CD4 + T cells modulates early effector responses in colorectal cancer
items.abstract: Strategies to improve cancer immunotherapy have largely focused on the intratumor immunosuppressive microenvironment, whereas approaches to amplify peripheral T cells and promote tumor recruitment have not been thoroughly explored. Using imaging mass cytometry in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC), we observed T helper 1 (T H 1)–like immune architectures in mismatch repair–deficient tumors associated with response to anti–programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) immunotherapy. By contrast, mismatch repair–proficient (pMMR) tumors showed regulatory T–dominant spatial interactions. Clonal analyses revealed that stem-like CD4 + T cells differentiated into T H 1-like cells after PD-1 blockade. In pMMR CRC mouse models, combined OX40 agonist and PD-1 blockade suppressed tumor progression by expanding Il7r + early effector CD4 + intermediates in tumor-draining lymph nodes, promoting migration and connection with T H 1-like cells. This was accompanied by interferon-γ–dependent induction of immunostimulatory monocyte-macrophages and CD8 + effector T cells. These findings suggest that leveraging peripheral CD4 + T cell amplification may improve immunotherapy responses.

items.title: Increased demographic turnover and isolation precede social fragmentation in Asian elephants
items.abstract: Humans and many other animals live in interconnected social communities that are essential for survival and well-being. In principle, communities can persist despite changes in constituent members. However, gradually accumulating changes to membership could push systems past critical thresholds into alternate states, restructuring patterns of connectivity. Such changes can further affect systemic resilience against disturbance. We investigated social network dynamics for 443 wild female Asian elephants over 12 years by tracking community membership and structure. Following accumulated demographic turnover, networks fractured into smaller and more isolated communities. Connections changed not only owing to loss of members but also modifications in relationships among remaining individuals. This provides empirical evidence of a persistent state change in the social network of a long-lived terrestrial mammal following gradually accumulating demographic turnover.

items.title: Human replisomes direct a dedicated leading-strand primase for fork restart
items.abstract: Abstract Disruptions to leading-strand synthesis impair and stall replication forks because DNA synthesis by the leading-strand polymerase, Pol ε, is essential for optimal template unwinding by the replicative CMG (CDC45–MCM–GINS) helicase 1,2 . Failure to efficiently restart and/or protect stalled replication forks is a major source of genomic instability 3–6 . Stalled forks can be restarted by a variety of mechanisms, including repriming downstream of the impediment 4 . In human cells, the primase–polymerase PRIMPOL promotes fork progression during replication stress 7–10 , but how its activity is coordinated by the replisome is unresolved. Here, by reconstituting replication fork stalling and restart with purified human proteins, we show that the CMG helicase directs PRIMPOL for efficient replication fork restart. Unexpectedly, the interaction between PRIMPOL and replication protein A 9,11 is not critical for fork restart in this system. We show that PRIMPOL binds directly to CMG, and a cryo-electron microscopy structure illustrates how this targets PRIMPOL specifically for leading-strand priming to minimize the size of post-replicative gaps. Ablating the CMG–PRIMPOL interaction abolishes fork restart in vitro and PRIMPOL-dependent DNA damage tolerance in human cells. Our work establishes PRIMPOL as an integrated component of the human replisome dedicated to leading-strand priming.

items.title: Quantum-accurate enhanced sampling and mini-protein folding through replica exchange for multiscale neural network potentials.
items.abstract: Neural network potentials (NNPs) have emerged as efficient alternatives to computationally demanding quantum-mechanical (QM) methods. AMPv3-EE-BMS25 (short AMP-BMS) is an equivariant NNP designed for multiscale ML/MM simulations that captures directional and long-range interactions. In classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, enhanced-sampling techniques are applied to cross large energy barriers and improve convergence. Among those, replica exchange with solute tempering (REST2) is an efficient method that selectively scales solute interactions while keeping the bath temperature fixed, thereby reducing the number of replicas required. Here, we present a REST2-like algorithm compatible with multiscale ML/MM simulations. This algorithm is combined with AMP-BMS by exploiting the separability of its Hamiltonian into solute-solute, solute-solvent, and solvent-solvent contributions. We validate the REST2-AMP approach on several peptidic systems in explicit solvent and demonstrate folding of the mini-proteins chignolin and CLN025 from extended conformations. Thus, our REST2 approach for ML/MM enables access to biologically relevant timescales while maintaining near-DFT accuracy.

items.title: TMEM184 proteins are Ca2+ uptake transporters in lysosomes
Non-equilibrium resonance scattering in intramolecular charge transport drives conformational changes
items.abstract: Abstract Intramolecular charge transport is conventionally described as proceeding along a static ground-state potential, with the carrier acting as a passive probe of a fixed electronic landscape. Here, using alkanethiolate-based molecular junctions, we show that the carrier itself can drive conformational reorganization once the applied bias brings backbone-delocalized molecular orbitals into the transmission window. Combined electrical and in situ structural measurements resolve a threshold-activated transition to a gauche-defect state coincident with the onset of orbital-mediated transport. We rationalize this coupling through a quantum resonance scattering framework in which accessible orbitals act as scattering potentials that transiently host the injected charge, depositing energy into nuclear motion with an efficiency set by molecule–electrode coupling and Franck–Condon overlap. The framework quantitatively reproduces the measured response and predicts the enhanced behavior of amide-containing junctions. Together, these results suggest that charge-transport–structure feedback can be understood in terms of microscopic parameters governing resonance-mediated energy transfer, and that these parameters may be tuned through chemical design.

items.title: AS01E-adjuvanted RSV pre-F protein vaccine in adults with lung or kidney transplant: a phase 2b randomized trial
items.abstract: Abstract Immunocompromised adults are at increased risk of severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease. This multicountry, open-label phase 2b trial (NCT05921903) evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of the AS01 E -adjuvanted RSV prefusion F protein vaccine (adjuvanted RSVPreF3) over 12 months in kidney or lung transplant recipients ≥18 years, randomized 1:1 to receive one ( n = 131) or two doses 30–60 days apart ( n = 130). A control group of non-immunocompromised adults ≥50 years ( n = 125) received a single dose. The primary outcome was the mean geometric increase in RSV-A and RSV-B neutralizing titers one month following a second adjuvanted RSVPreF3 dose relative to the first dose in transplant recipients. Secondary outcomes included assessment of the safety and immunogenicity of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in transplant recipients compared with the control group. In transplant recipients receiving two doses, neutralizing titers against RSV-A and RSV-B were numerically higher one month post-dose 2 than post-dose 1 (mean geometric increases: 1.34 [95% CI: 1.20, 1.48] for RSV-A [ n = 111] and 1.26 [95% CI: 1.14, 1.40] for RSV-B [ n = 111]). A single dose was immunogenic in transplant recipients, but showed slower and generally lower initial neutralizing responses than in non-immunocompromised controls, specifically in individuals receiving mycophenolate. RSVPreF3-specific CD4 + T-cell frequencies increased after vaccination versus baseline in all groups. items.title: Humanized yeast ORC drives R-loop dependent transcription-replication conflicts and global gene dysregulation
items.abstract: Abstract The Origin Recognition Complex (ORC) recruits Mini-Chromosome Maintenance (MCM) hexamers to initiate eukaryotic DNA replication. While yeast ORC binds specific DNA motifs, human ORC binds sequence-agnostically nucleosome-depleted promoter regions. Here, using a mutant yeast model that recapitulates the human ORC binding landscape, we demonstrate that pervasive and unscheduled ORC binding at promoters in the compact yeast genome generates R-loop associated transcription-replication conflicts and disrupts gene expression across thousands of genes. Unexpectedly, we also uncover that substituting endogenous gene promoters with a replication origin sequence maintains robust transcription. We reveal that this intrinsic, promoter-like function relies on the ability of origins to form a nucleosome-depleted region (NDR) encoded within the origin’s sequence composition. However, origin-substituted loci reposition the +1 nucleosome which drives the transcription machinery to select alternative transcription start sites (TSSs). Thus, origins and promoters share an intrinsic chromatin structure-controlled ability to drive transcription initiation. Together, our results show that origin licensing in compact genomes relies on sequence-specific, coupled origin licensing to insulate transcription from the replication machinery.

items.title: Coiled Coils as a Programmable Platform for Computational Biosensor Design.
items.abstract: Coiled coils are a versatile class of α-helical protein motifs characterized by recurring sequence patterns that direct their assembly into defined oligomeric bundles and underpin a wide range of biological functions. The well-established sequence-structure relationships governing coiled-coil formation enable predictive control over stability, specificity, and oligomerization state, making them attractive and chemically tractable building blocks for biosensor design in applications ranging from single-molecule detection to synthetic biochemical circuits and functional nanomaterials. After revisiting the theoretical foundations of coiled-coil architecture, this review outlines strategies to engineer programmable binding interfaces that can be rationally tuned to generate orthogonal, high-affinity interaction pairs, enabling flexible and modular biosensor platforms. Particular emphasis is placed on recent advances in computational and data-driven design approaches, including machine-learning and AI-based strategies, alongside established rational and empirical methods for coiled-coil construction. These complementary design principles underpin the development of coiled-coil-based biosensors and are discussed together with selected application examples to illustrate how engineered coiled-coil interactions support sensitive and specific molecular recognition as well as switchable control in synthetic biology and chemical biology. Depth-enhanced molecular imaging with two-photon oblique plane microscopy
items.abstract: Abstract High-numerical-aperture (NA) oblique plane microscopy enables noninvasive fluorescence imaging of subcellular dynamics without radical sample modification. However, performance degrades at depth in multicellular specimens as scattering and refractive-index heterogeneity raise out-of-focus background. We report a two-photon oblique plane microscope that improves resolution at depth by combining high-NA single-objective detection with multiphoton plane illumination. The microscope achieves ~ 300 nm lateral and ~ 650 nm axial resolution, with single-molecule sensitivity and 5 × faster volumetric acquisition (up to 3.25 × 10 6 voxels s −1 ). In multicellular contexts, near-infrared nonlinear excitation enhances contrast throughout the illumination depth by ~ 2 × and restores volumetric resolving power by > 2 × relative to linear excitation. We demonstrate these capabilities through molecular imaging of epithelial tissue, stem-cell-derived gastruloids, and living fruit fly embryos, including multicolor transcription-factor dynamics, optogenetic subcellular control, and single-mRNA tracking, all using standard glass-based mounting.

Strain-induced correlated metallic phase in 1T-TaS2
items.abstract: Abstract Layered transition-metal dichalcogenide 1T-TaS 2 has long been considered a prime example of a Mott insulator driven by strong electron correlations. However, this view has been recently challenged by proposals which favor a band insulating state arising from interlayer dimerization. This ongoing debate opens a frontier in 1T-TaS 2 research focusing on stacking order, and raises a fundamental question with broad implications for two-dimensional materials: can electronic phases be engineered by actively tuning interlayer coupling? Here, using micro-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy supported by first-principles calculations, we demonstrate that uniaxial strain drives 1T-TaS 2 from its insulating charge-density-wave phase into a stable metallic phase. This metallic phase, distinct from hydrostatic-pressure-induced or non-equilibrium hidden phases, emerges via a strain-induced rearrangement in the interlayer stacking of the Star-of-David charge order, effectively disrupting interlayer dimerization. Furthermore, the emergent metallic phase exhibits a significant quasiparticle mass renormalization, a hallmark of strong electron correlations, indicating its correlated nature and proximity to a Mott instability. This finding necessitates a re-evaluation of the interplay between structural and strong correlations in 1T-TaS 2 . The present results establish uniaxial strain as a powerful method for tuning the interlayer coupling, opening pathways for exploring quantum phases inaccessible under ambient conditions.

Sugar rationing during the first 1000 days of life and biological aging and age-related diseases
items.abstract: Abstract Early-life nutritional conditions may influence biological aging and age-related health, but the long-term associations of early exposure to sugar rationing remain unclear. Here we investigate the associations of early-life exposure to sugar rationing with biological aging and age-related diseases among 54,201 participants in the UK Biobank, taking advantage of the abrupt end of post-war sugar rationing as a natural experiment. Exposure to sugar rationing during the first 1000 days of life is associated with lower biological age acceleration, with stronger associations observed among participants with longer exposure durations. The association is more pronounced in females and remains consistent across strata of genetic susceptibility. Early-life exposure to sugar rationing is also associated with lower risks of age-related cataract and chronic kidney disease, but not with several other age-related diseases examined. Overall, these findings suggest that early-life exposure to a population-level nutritional policy is associated with biological aging and several age-related diseases in later life, highlighting the potential long-term relevance of early-life nutritional environments for healthy aging.

items.title: Room-temperature continuous-wave lasing-like emission from solution-processed bulk monolayer MoS2 thin films
items.abstract: Abstract Monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) are promising laser-gain media for their direct bandgap and strong excitonic effects. However, existing TMD lasers typically rely on mechanically exfoliated or high-temperature chemical-vapor-deposition-grown materials, with their atomic-scale thickness inherently limiting the available optical gain volume. Here, we report room-temperature continuous-wave lasing-like emission from solution-processed bulk monolayer MoS 2 (BM-MoS 2 ) thin films in whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) cavities. Using solution exfoliation and spray coating under ambient conditions, we produce area- and thickness-scalable BM-MoS 2 films composed of electronically decoupled MoS 2 monolayers separated by organic spacers. This layered architecture preserves the intrinsic monolayer excitonic properties while providing a tunable gain volume beyond that of an isolated monolayer. Integrated with WGM cavities, the thickness-scalable BM-MoS 2 films enable a balance between the quality ( Q ) and optical confinement ( $$\varGamma$$ Γ ) factors. Power-dependent measurements reveal key lasing signatures, including a threshold-like input-output crossover accompanied by linewidth narrowing at a pump power of approximately 1.4 nW, and pump-induced polarization selection. Solution-processable BM-MoS 2 thus offers a scalable gain medium for thin-film laser photonics.

A microfluidic fluorescence lifetime screening platform bridges in vitro and in vivo formats and enables discovery of Amyloid β aggregation inhibitors
items.abstract: Abstract Inhibiting the aggregation of Amyloid β (1-42) is a promising strategy for the development of disease-modifying Alzheimer’s disease therapeutics. To date, however, no sufficiently efficacious inhibitors have been identified, despite the best efforts of more than 200 advanced drug development campaigns. This failure can be partially attributed to limitations in current in vitro compound screening and in vivo validation assays. Here, we report a high throughput assay platform based on the use of a fluorescence lifetime aggregation sensor that can be applied in vitro and in vivo. This microfluidic “nanoFLIM” assay presents a cost-effective and reliable alternative to conventional early-stage small molecule discovery platforms for cell-free Amyloid β aggregation. The fluorescence lifetime sensor can dynamically monitor peptide aggregation in cellular and Caenorhabditis elegans disease models, providing directly comparable aggregation kinetics, which is not achievable by any other method. The power of this unified platform for accelerating hit-to-lead strategies, lowering attrition rates and expediting in vivo screening, was demonstrated with a pilot screening campaign of 445 compounds, revealing an inhibitor that can inhibit Amyloid β self-assembly both in vitro as well as in cellular and whole organism disease models.

De Novo Design of Multi-Mechanistic AIE Photosensitizer for Broad-Spectrum Bacterial Eradication.
items.abstract: Antibiotic resistance poses a serious threat to human health. Inspired by the clinical practice of employing drug combinations to achieve combined effects, we hypothesized that integrating multiple mechanisms into a single molecule could address drug-resistant bacterial infections. Based on a propeller-modification strategy and dual alkyl-chain engineering, we de novo designed and synthesized a C2-symmetric propeller-shaped aggregation-induced emission photosensitizer. After iterative screening, the optimized compound MeOTDP-2 exhibits broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, enabling efficient eradication of planktonic bacteria, drug-resistant strains, polymicrobial infections, biofilms, and persister cells, with no cellular invasiveness and negligible cytotoxicity. Mechanistic studies revealed that MeOTDP-2 achieves chemo-photodynamic combined antibacterial therapy by targeting and disrupting bacterial membranes and DNA, alongside light-mediated intracellular reactive oxygen species accumulation. Furthermore, in mouse models of MRSA-induced skin abscess and full-thickness skin wound infection, MeOTDP-2 demonstrated superior therapeutic efficacy to vancomycin. This strategy, integrating dual targeting with multiple mechanisms, offers new promise for overcoming bacterial resistance.
